news.title: London’s Bloomsbury Institute loses licence to sponsor international students
news.summary_en: The Bloomsbury Institute has had its licence to sponsor international students revoked after failing to meet the Basic Compliance Assessment, the Home Office has confirmed in a statement.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Korea lets universities set own language tests in latest internationalisation push
news.summary_en: IEQAS-certified universities will be able to assess applicants' Korean proficiency themselves as Seoul seeks to widen access while tightening oversight of international recruitment.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: How to get the most from Erasmus+
news.summary_en: With the return of Erasmus+ in 2027, many institutions will focus on funding opportunities, but this is only one part of the story, writes Kate Erskine.
news.author: Kate Erskine

news.title: US leaders urge action as delays threaten fall enrolments
news.summary_en: Higher education leaders in the US are urging policymakers to demand visa processing improvements, as delays threaten to wreak havoc on this fall’s international enrolments.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: US set to expand exchange visitor termination rules
news.summary_en: US proposals to expand exchange visitor termination rules appear to be a routine regulatory update, though some stakeholders remain wary of the rule's wording.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Chinese group to buy Kaplan’s Dublin Business School in $125.5m deal
news.summary_en: China Chunlai Education Group Co is set to acquire Dublin Business School (DBS) from Kaplan in a deal worth a reported USD$127.5 million.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: QQI unveils first TrustEd Ireland Quality Mark recipients
news.summary_en: Quality and Qualifications Ireland (QQI) has announced the first English Language Education (ELE) providers authorised to use the TrustEd Ireland Quality Mark, a new statutory accreditation program designed to strengthen quality assurance and support the protection of international students.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Universities and test providers debate access to English language test responses
news.summary_en: A growing trend among some English language testing providers to give university admissions teams access to candidates' spoken responses has sparked debate over whether greater transparency improves admissions decisions.
news.author: Amy Baker

news.title: US universities sell opportunity. A $100k OPT fee could change the product
news.summary_en: News that the Trump administration is eyeing a $100,000 fee for OPT poses a serious risk to US international education, warns Richard T. Herman.
news.author: Richard T. Herman
